thread:
maria: Thinking about batch slice granularity — rough proposal: bucket microbatches by token-length and allow limited fanout to adjacent GPU lanes to avoid eviction storms from long tails. Thoughts?

aj: Can you sketch the latency vs throughput tradeoffs? Fanout sounds useful but worried about extra memcpy and KV pressure.

noah: If we allow fanout we must pin KV-cache per-slice or we risk evicting an entire tenant because of one long sequence. Hysteresis on evictions helps.

sasha: Sketch of config I'm picturing:```json
{
  "slice_policy": "len_histogram",
  "bucket_bounds_tokens": [64, 256, 1024],
  "max_fanout": 2,
  "evict_hysteresis_ms": 200,
  "min_slot_reserve_per_tenant": 1
}```Keep defaults conservative.

infra-bot: PR opened: https://git.local/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4123 — initial slice/fanout prototype (WIP).

aj: Main runtime risk is headroom fragmentation. If slices steal fastpath slots p50 will regress. We need an enforceable minimum reserve per GPU or per-lane.

maria: Agreed. Proposal: reserve = max(min_slots_per_tenant, ceil(active_tenants * fraction_of_slots)) and enforce at admission. Use `min_slots_per_tenant`=1 as safe default.

noah: Observability needs: `slice_fanout_count`, `eviction_wave_size`, `kv_pin_ratio`, `slice_queue_fill_pct`. Also add tracing spans for slice join/leave so we can see fanout latency cost.

sasha: Also backpressure propagation: if slice queue saturates upstream should attach a deadline-hint so coalescer can avoid waiting for that slice. Otherwise we create long tail latency for everyone. :exclamation:

aj: +1. I'll run a sim with a workload mix: 80% short (10-50 tokens), 10% medium (200-400), 10% long (>1k). Want to compare synchronous duplicate vs pointer-based fanout.

maria: Nice. Can you include memory and memcpy counts in the sim? Also measure KV churn (pins/unpins per second).

aj: Yep, will add `memcpy_bytes`, `gpu_mem_shared_pointers`, `kv_pin_ops` to metrics. Target to have sim results by EOD Thursday.

aj: Quick question — should fanout be synchronous (duplicate payloads sent to multiple lanes) or pointer-based (shared input refs)? Pointer-based is nicer for CPU mem but harder for GPU/buffer management.

noah: My vote: pointer-based for inputs, but copy-on-write semantics for KV contexts. For long tails we can duplicate KV only when mutation/eviction risk appears. I'll prototype pointer+COW.

maria: Good plan. Follow-ups: I'll draft a lightweight RFC that contains config options + telemetry checklist + safe defaults: `max_fanout=1`, `evict_hysteresis_ms=250`, `reserve_slots_fraction=0.1`. We'll iterate after sims. @aj please attach sim artifacts to the RFC.

aj: :thumbsup: will do.

sasha: One more nit — rollout strategy: gated rollout behind `runtime.feature.slice_fanout` with canary on low-traffic hosts, and `eviction_hysteresis` telemetry alert to auto-disable if `eviction_wave_size > 5` within 1m.

maria: Agree. Thanks all — very actionable. I'll create RFC and a follow-up thread for telemetry dashboards.
